extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing creative writers (novelists, poets, essayists) and students of writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creative writers about how to conceive the writer-self and practical/value-based criteria for producing literary work — addressing relationship to tradition, audience, commerce, and mortality. Useful for authors shaping voice, vocation, and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation: Who do you think you are?
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-conception of 'writer' — how a writer understands their role, identity, and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writer must reflect on what it means to be a writer; this self-conception shapes choices of subject, voice, and stance. Anti-pattern: adopting an unexamined or conventional identity that constrains authenticity or blinds the writer to responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicity / The Doubled Self
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'I' who lives and the 'I' who writes are not identical; the writer-self is a constructed, partial fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and use the split between living self and writing self — the writer-self can be cultivated, dramatized, or distanced. Guidance implies avoiding the assumption that the narrative voice simply transcribes life; instead, treat voice as an artful negotiation. Anti-pattern: collapsing the two selves and confusing personal biography with literary voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedication: The Great God Pen (Vocation and Ambition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing as vocation, calling, or committed craft requiring dedication and seriousness of purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate writing by the degree of dedication — persistence, discipline, and willingness to accept the demands of craft. Consider ambition and the ethical dimension of pursuing a literary life. Anti-patterns include casualness, opportunism, or treating writing only as a hobby without professional rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temptation: Art vs. Commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mephistopheles theme — the trade-offs and risks when entering the marketplace; balancing artistic integrity with commercial pressures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess choices (tone, form, subject, marketing) in light of whether they serve the work or merely marketability. Strive to 'keep faith with the work' while navigating financial and professional realities. Anti-pattern: compromising essential truth or craft for short-term commercial gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communion: Relationship Between Writer and Reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing as an act of communion — building an imagined or absent readerly counterpart; the dialogic relationship between writer and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of whom you are addressing (real, imagined, future readers) and shape tone, clarity, and empathy accordingly. Effective work creates a sense of exchange; avoid solipsism or opacity that shuts readers out. Examples: constructing an 'ideal reader' to focus decisions; anti-patterns include ignoring reader comprehension or emotional engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descent: Negotiating with the Dead (Tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every writer writes within and against tradition; texts speak to texts. The writer mediates between predecessors (the dead) and the living (readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good writing engages tradition consciously rather than naively — acknowledge influences, echo or subvert predecessors, and negotiate lineage. Criteria include awareness of antecedents, intertextuality used thoughtfully, and an original positioning relative to tradition. Anti-pattern: derivative work that fails to acknowledge or transform its sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Ideal Reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing and addressing an absent or constructed reader (the dead, the future, an imagined kindred spirit) to guide tone and choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define an imagined reader to clarify diction, level of explanation, and moral framing. Use this construct to calibrate intimacy and distance. Anti-pattern: writing without any reader in mind, resulting in either over-explanation or inaccessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Female Writer's Particular Burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledges additional historical and social pressures faced by women writers, including assumptions that the writer-self is male.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing work by women, consider how gendered expectations shape voice, subject choice, and reception. Be alert to biases that marginalize or misread female-authored texts. Anti-pattern: applying male-normative standards uncritically or erasing gendered context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage Tradition Consciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Great writing engages tradition consciously, not naively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work shows awareness of literary history and deliberately positions itself in relation to it — through homage, revision, parody, or critique. Look for evidence that the author has thought about predecessors and made deliberate choices about influence and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice as Construction, Not Transcription
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer's voice is constructed, not transcribed from life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the craft behind voice: consistency, intentionality, range, and appropriateness to material. Strong work exhibits deliberate shaping of narrative persona rather than careless or accidental tone. Anti-pattern: treating voice as mere reportage of the self.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-Awareness Without Compromise of Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience-awareness shapes tone but shouldn't compromise truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance sensitivity to readers with fidelity to the work's integrity — avoid pandering or self-censorship that dulls truth. Good decisions consider accessibility and honesty simultaneously. Anti-pattern: altering essential content or perspective primarily to please market expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confronting Mortality / What's Been Lost / What Survives
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing requires confronting mortality and the traces of the past — what is lost and what endures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate depth of engagement with themes of loss, memory, and history; strong work shows courage to face difficult truths about mortality and legacy. Anti-pattern: sentimentality that avoids real reckoning with loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations Beyond the Moment
rubrics_metrics.description: The work has obligations beyond the moment of writing — to tradition, readers, and future interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how a piece will resonate over time and its responsibilities to cultural memory. Criteria include durability of insight, ethical seriousness, and resistance to fleeting trends. Anti-pattern: ephemeral or gimmicky work with little lasting relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to Look (Curiosity and Attention)
rubrics_metrics.description: The thing that's needed in the writer is the willingness to look.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess attentiveness: the author's capacity for observation, scrutiny, and moral/empathetic vision. Strong writing demonstrates curiosity and detailed perception. Anti-patterns: complacency, laziness, or avoidance of difficult subjects.
